newsitem.title: USA: Court rejects Colgate tax proposal - NYTimes.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects Colgate tax proposal - NYTimes.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Tax Court has rejected a plan by Merrill Lynch that enabled Colgate-Palmolive Co to avoid taxes on $98 million it made from selling a subsidiary, the New York Times said Friday.
The paper said the court ruled the manuever had no "economic substance," and that Colgate was motivated by a desire to avoid taxes.

The paper said similar deals designed by Merrill Lynch for other companies had been challenged by the Internal Revenue Service, but the Colgate transaction was the first decision by a court on the issue.
The report said the plan involved a partnership owned by Colgate, Dutch bank ABN AMRO Holding and Merrill Lynch, which bought some Citibank notes in 1989 and sold most of the notes later that year.

Using a section of the tax law, the partnership allocated only part of the cost of the notes to the ones sold, thus creating a large paper profit that was mostly allocated to ABN AMRO, the report said.

ABN AMRO left the partnership, and the later sale on the rest of the notes created a paper loss, the paper said. It said most of the losses were allocated to Colgate, which applied to use them to recover taxes previously paid on profit from the sale of a subsidiary.
Colgate told the paper the ruling would have no effect on its cash position or reported profits.
